Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: Solve the following equations, giving exact solutions: (a) $$\ln(2x-5)=8$$ (b) $$e^{4x}=5$$ (c) $$24-e^{-2x}=10$$ (d) $$\ln x+\ln(x-3)=0$$ (e) $$e^{x}+e^{-x}=2$$ (f) $$\ln2+\ln x=4$$.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: Rewrite logs/exponentials, isolate $$x$$ using $$e^{\ln y}=y$$ and standard algebra; for (e) set $$u=e^{x}$$.
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$(a)\ \ln(2x-5)=8\Rightarrow2x-5=e^{8}\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{e^{8}+5}{2}.$$ $$(b)\ e^{4x}=5\Rightarrow4x=\ln5\Rightarrow x=\tfrac14\ln5.$$ $$(c)\ 24-e^{-2x}=10\Rightarrow e^{-2x}=14\Rightarrow-2x=\ln14\Rightarrow x=-\tfrac12\ln14.$$ $$(d)\ \ln x+\ln(x-3)=\ln[x(x-3)]=0\Rightarrow x(x-3)=1\Rightarrow x^{2}-3x-1=0,$$ $$x=\dfrac{3\pm\sqrt{13}}{2},\ \text{but domain }x>3\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{3+\sqrt{13}}{2}.$$ $$(e)\ e^{x}+e^{-x}=2;\ \text{let }u=e^{x}\Rightarrow u+\dfrac1u=2\Rightarrow u^{2}-2u+1=0\Rightarrow(u-1)^{2}=0\Rightarrow u=1,$$ $$e^{x}=1\Rightarrow x=0.$$ $$(f)\ \ln2+\ln x=\ln(2x)=4\Rightarrow2x=e^{4}\Rightarrow x=\tfrac12e^{4}.$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: The price of a computer system is modelled by $$P=100+850e^{-t/2}$$ (in £) where $$t$$ is the age in years. (a) Find the new price. (b) Find the price after 3 years. (c) Find when it will be worth less than £200. (d) Find its price as $$t\to\infty$$. (e) Sketch the graph of $$P$$ against $$t$$. Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$(a)\ P(0)=100+850e^{0}=950. \quad (b)\ P(3)=100+850e^{-3/2}\approx289.7\ (\text{about }£290).$$ $$(c)\ 100+850e^{-t/2}<200\Rightarrow850e^{-t/2}<100\Rightarrow e^{-t/2}<\tfrac{2}{17}\Rightarrow-\tfrac{t}{2}<\ln\tfrac{2}{17}\Rightarrow t>2\ln\tfrac{17}{2}\approx4.28\ \text{years}.$$ $$(d)\ \lim_{t\to\infty}P=100+850\cdot0=100. \quad (e)\ \text{Decreasing exponential curve from }(0,950)\text{ towards the horizontal asymptote }P=100\text{ as }t\to\infty.$$ $$(f)\ \text{Reasonable for early years, but in reality the price might eventually fall below }£100\text{ or drop suddenly, so the long-term behaviour of the model is not fully realistic.}$$

$$\text{Data follows }y=ax^n.\ (a)\ \text{Complete the table of }\log x\text{ and }\log y\text{ (2 d.p.).}\  !{}(14h_3a.png)  (b)\ \text{Plot }\log y\text{ vs }\log x\text{ and draw a best-fit line.}\ (c)\ \text{Estimate }a\text{ and }n\text{ (1 d.p.).}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\log y&=\log a+n\log x\\ \text{Gradient }&=n,\ \text{Intercept }=\log a\\ \text{From best-fit: }&n\approx1.5,\ a\approx2.1\ (\text{est.})\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{Data follows }y=ab^x.\ (a)\ \text{Complete the table of }\log y\text{ (2 d.p.).}\  !{}(14h_4a.png) (b)\ \text{Plot }\log y\text{ vs }x\text{ and draw a best-fit line.}\ (c)\ \text{Estimate }a\text{ and }b\text{ (1 d.p.).}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\log y&=\log a+x\log b\\ \text{Gradient }&=\log b,\ \text{Intercept }=\log a\\ \text{From best-fit: }&b\approx1.9,\ a\approx30.0\ (\text{est.})\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{Kleiber's law states }R=am^b,\ \text{where }R\text{ is resting metabolic rate and }m\text{ is mass. Given data for five animals: (a) copy and complete a table of }\log m\text{ and }\log R\text{ (2 d.p.). !{}(14h_5a.png) (b) plot }\log R\text{ against }\log m\text{ and draw a line of best fit. (c) estimate }a\text{ and }b\text{ (2 s.f.). (d) estimate }R\text{ for a human of mass }80\text{ kg.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: $$\text{Take logs: }\log R=\log a+b\log m;\ \text{use gradient and intercept of straight-line graph.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{(a)}\ &\log m=(-1.52,-0.39,0.62,1.54,2.81),\\ &\log R=(0.62,1.51,2.29,2.88,3.88)\\[4pt]\text{(b)}\ &\log R=b\log m+\log a\\[4pt]\text{(c)}\ &b\approx0.75,\ \log a\approx1.40\Rightarrow a\approx25\\[4pt]\text{(d)}\ &R=25(80)^{0.75}\approx670\ \text{kcal/day}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{Zipf's law: }f=AR^b.\ \text{Data (per }10{,}000\text{ words): }(R,f)=(1,4897),(10,861),(100,92),(1000,9).\ (a)\ \text{Complete table of }\log f\text{ (2 d.p.) for }\log R=0,1,2,3.\  !{}(14h_6a.png) (b)\ \text{Plot }\log f\text{ against }\log R\text{ and draw best-fit line.}\ (c)\ \text{Estimate }A\text{ (2 s.f.) and }b\text{ (1 d.p.).}\ (d)\ \text{If rank }57\text{ word appears in a }455125\text{-word trilogy, estimate how many times it appears.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: $$\text{Take logs: }\log f=\log A+b\log R;\ \text{use straight-line gradient }b\text{ and intercept }\log A.$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{(a)}\ &\log R=(0,1,2,3)\\ &\log f=(\log4897,\log861,\log92,\log9)\approx(3.69,2.94,1.96,0.95)\\[4pt]\text{(b)}\ &\log f=\log A+b\log R\\[4pt]\text{(c)}\ &b\approx-0.92\approx-0.9\ (1\text{ d.p.}),\ \log A\approx3.76\Rightarrow A\approx10^{3.76}\approx5.8\times10^3\\[4pt]\text{(d)}\ &f(57)=A\cdot57^{\,b}\approx(5.8\times10^3)\cdot57^{-0.92}\approx1.42\times10^2\\ &\text{Expected count }=\frac{455125}{10000}\,f(57)\approx45.5125\times141.5\approx6.44\times10^3\approx6400\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{Mozambique population (millions): }(t,P)=(0,7.6),(10,9.5),(20,12.1),(30,13.6),(40,18.3),(50,23.4),\ \text{where }t\text{ is years since 1960. Model }P=ab^t.\ (a)\ \text{Complete table of }\log P\text{ (2 d.p.).}\  $$\text{Zipf's law: }f=AR^b.\ \text{Data (per }10{,}000\text{ words): }(R,f)=(1,4897),(10,861),(100,92),(1000,9).\ (a)\ \text{Complete table of }\log f\text{ (2 d.p.) for }\log R=0,1,2,3.\  !{}(14h_67.png) (b)\ \text{Plot }\log f\text{ against }\log R\text{ and draw best-fit line.}\ (c)\ \text{Estimate }A\text{ (2 s.f.) and }b\text{ (1 d.p.).}\ (d)\ \text{If rank }57\text{ word appears in a }455125\text{-word trilogy, estimate how many times it appears.}$$(b)\ \text{Show }\log P=\log a+t\log b.\ (c)\ \text{Plot }\log P\text{ against }t\text{ and draw best-fit line.}\ (d)\ \text{Estimate }a\text{ and }b.\ (e)\ \text{Explain why an exponential model is often appropriate for population.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: $$\text{Linearise with logs: }\log P=\log a+t\log b;\ \text{gradient}=\log b,\ \text{intercept}=\log a.$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{(a)}\ &\log P=(\log7.6,\log9.5,\log12.1,\log13.6,\log18.3,\log23.4)\\ &\approx(0.88,0.98,1.08,1.13,1.26,1.37)\ \text{(2 d.p.)}\\[4pt]\text{(b)}\ &P=ab^t\Rightarrow \log P=\log(ab^t)=\log a+\log(b^t)=\log a+t\log b\\[4pt]\text{(c)}\ &\text{Best-fit line: }\log P=mt+c\ \text{with }m=\log b,\ c=\log a\\[4pt]\text{(d)}\ &m\approx0.00956\Rightarrow b=10^{m}\approx10^{0.00956}\approx1.022\approx1.02\\ &c\approx0.879\Rightarrow a=10^{c}\approx10^{0.879}\approx7.56\approx7.6\\ &\Rightarrow P\approx7.6(1.02)^t\\[4pt]\text{(e)}\ &\text{If growth rate is roughly proportional to current population, } \frac{dP}{dt}\propto P,\ \text{giving exponential growth.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{A scientist models the number of sick people }N\text{ after }t\text{ days. A graph of }\log N\text{ against }t\text{ is a straight line through }(0,1.6)\text{ and }(10,2.55).\ \text{The model is }N=ab^t.\ (a)\ \text{Find the equation of the line.}\ (b)\ \text{Find }a\text{ and }b\text{ (2 s.f.).}\ (c)\ \text{Interpret }a.\ (d)\ \text{Predict }N\text{ after }30\text{ days and explain why this may be an overestimate.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.hint: $$\text{Use gradient }m=\frac{\Delta(\log N)}{\Delta t}\text{ and intercept }c;\ \log N=mt+c.\ \text{Then }a=10^c,\ b=10^m.$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{(a)}\ m&=\frac{2.55-1.60}{10}=0.095,\quad c=1.60\\ \Rightarrow\ \log N&=0.095t+1.60\\[4pt]\text{(b)}\ N&=10^{\log N}=10^{1.60}\cdot 10^{0.095t}\\ \Rightarrow\ a&=10^{1.60}\approx39.81\approx4.0\times10^{1}\ (\text{2 s.f.})\\ b&=10^{0.095}\approx1.245\approx1.2\ (\text{2 s.f.})\\[4pt]\text{(c)}\ a&=\text{the predicted number sick at }t=0\ (\approx40\text{ people})\\[4pt]\text{(d)}\ \log N(30)&=0.095(30)+1.60=4.45\\ N(30)&=10^{4.45}\approx2.82\times10^{4}\approx2.8\times10^{4}\\ \text{Overestimate: }&\text{growth will not remain exponential due to finite population, immunity/recovery, interventions, and behavior changes.}\end{aligned}$$

Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.question_text: $$\text{A student investigates a family of similar shapes. She measures width }w\text{ and area }A,\ \text{and plots }\log A\text{ against }\log w.\ \text{The graph has gradient }2\text{ and y-intercept }-0.1049.\ (a)\ \text{Write the equation of the line.}\ (b)\ \text{Find the exact values of }q\text{ and }p.\ (c)\ \text{Suggest the family of shapes and justify.}$$
Chapter 14 - Exponentials and log.correct_answer: $$\begin{aligned}\text{(a)}\ \log A&=2\log w-0.1049\\[4pt]\text{(b)}\ q&=2,\quad \log p=-0.1049\Rightarrow p=10^{-0.1049}\approx0.785\\ \text{Exact: }&0.785\approx\frac{\pi}{4}\Rightarrow p=\frac{\pi}{4}\\ \Rightarrow\ A&=\frac{\pi}{4}w^2\\[4pt]\text{(c)}\ &\text{Circles, with }w=\text{diameter }d:\ A=\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2=\frac{\pi}{4}d^2=\frac{\pi}{4}w^2\end{aligned}$$
